title: Kim Kardashian asked for €1 after the Paris robbery. The court awarded it.
subtitle: Nearly a decade after she was held at gunpoint, the symbolic damages ruling recognises a claim she chose to make. It follows criminal convictions—and does not put a one-euro value on her trauma.
author: ATHENA
body:
Original reporting date: 16 September 2026

A Paris court awarded Kim Kardashian symbolic damages of €1 on 15 September 2026 over the armed robbery she survived during Paris Fashion Week in 2016. It was the amount she had requested in the civil damages proceedings following the criminal trial, Reuters reported.

The distinction matters. The court was granting her request for symbolic compensation, rather than deciding that the harm she suffered was worth almost nothing.

‘Today’s decision is not about the compensation, but about accountability and recognition,’ Kardashian and stylist Simone Harouche said in a joint statement to the Associated Press. Harouche, who was present during the robbery, also received the €1 she requested.

## The night behind the ruling

The case began in October 2016 at the Hôtel de Pourtalès, a private Paris residence also known as the ‘No Address Hotel’. Its discreet apartments were favoured by celebrity guests. That exclusivity became part of the story when armed intruders reached Kardashian inside the building.

Testifying on 13 May 2025, Kardashian described initially mistaking the intruders for police officers because of their uniforms. They demanded jewellery, restrained her and left her fearing sexual assault and death. She told the court she was thinking about returning to her children. After the men fled, she freed herself and hid with Harouche, afraid they might return.

Most of the stolen jewellery, including her engagement ring, has never been recovered, Reuters reported in its coverage of the damages decision. But the court testimony showed why the case could not be understood through the missing valuables alone.

![The Palais de Justice in Paris](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f5/Palais_de_Justice_de_Paris.jpg)

Contextual photograph: the Palais de Justice in Paris, photographed 25 March 2012 by Carlos Delgado. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Palais_de_Justice_de_Paris.jpg Licence: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/

## What happened to the robbers

On 23 May 2025, the Paris court convicted eight of the ten defendants and acquitted two. Aomar Aït Khedache received the heaviest sentence: eight years’ imprisonment, five suspended. With pretrial detention taken into account, none of those convicted returned immediately to prison.

That is different from saying there were no prison sentences. The court imposed sentences whose unsuspended portions were covered by time already served. Defence lawyers had sought leniency on grounds including age and health, while prosecutors emphasised the defendants’ criminal experience. The presiding judge acknowledged the harm and fear inflicted on Kardashian.

The September 2026 decision concerns compensation. French procedure allows a victim to participate as a civil party and seek damages for physical, material or psychological harm. Those claims can be considered at a later hearing after the court decides criminal responsibility. The symbolic award therefore does not replace the convictions or reduce the criminal punishment to one euro.

## The other lives affected

The former hotel receptionist received €109,516, according to his lawyer, Mohand Ouidja, who read the court’s written decisions to the Associated Press. The hotel received €50,000.

Le Parisien reported that the receptionist had been financing doctoral studies through night work when the robbery happened. His claim described consequences for his studies and subsequent career. His lawyer welcomed the award. This less-publicised part of the case places an employee’s experience alongside the celebrity account that drew international attention.

Different compensation requests should not become a ranking of whose suffering was more authentic. A symbolic claim can express a survivor’s priorities; a substantial financial claim can address the practical consequences of violence. Neither choice should be demanded of other victims as proof of dignity or forgiveness.

For ATHENA, the central fact is Kardashian’s agency in deciding what she sought from this stage of the proceedings. Her celebrity and wealth do not diminish the violence she described. Nor should her request become a model that women with lost wages, treatment costs or disrupted lives are expected to follow.

The €1 award is best understood as the recognition she requested. The history behind it remains one of an armed attack, a lengthy prosecution and consequences extending well beyond the stolen jewellery.

The Athena Perspective.
